summary: Built hubreg, a standard-library Python package and CLI where every home-automation action is one record that drives call validation, refusals, assistant tool schemas, app controls, help text and a walker test. The binder fills defaults and checks types/units/limits/hooks, the diagnoser turns every failure into a refusal carrying valid names, the nearest name and a concrete fix (redirects and clamping come from the records), and the demo plug-ins (thermostat.set_temperature, light.dim, door.lock_door, scene.run_scene) exercise all three consumers. Tests cover registration structure and consistency, binding, refusals, confirmation, description, the walk, the CLI and record-generated limit/type/redirect cases; the last run was 155 tests, OK.

pattern_mapping.Operation record: hubreg/records.py: OpRecord (name, on, args, validate hook, fields/fields_for, flags, redirects, samples, doc, run), built and validated by build_record()
pattern_mapping.Argument spec: hubreg/records.py: ArgSpec (name, type, unit, default/optional, min/max, usual+usual_hint, values, redirects, doc), all values in the declared unit
pattern_mapping.Argument types (pluggable): hubreg/argtypes.py: ArgType interface (accepts/schema/describe) with Number/String/Bool/Enum; Registry.add_type(arg_types=...) plugs domain types without touching the binder
pattern_mapping.Flags: OpRecord.flags['confirm'] plus Registry.needs_confirmation(); the host set (confirm_required) OR the record flag, so a plug-in can add but never lower it
pattern_mapping.Registry: hubreg/registry.py: Registry.register / register_all, lookup, names/kinds/all, redirect_for, option_redirect, and delegation to binder/describer/diagnoser/walker
pattern_mapping.Binder: hubreg/binder.py: Binder.bind/bind_record — unknown-option check, defaults, type/range checks, usual-range warnings, cross-argument validate hook, then Call
pattern_mapping.Describer: hubreg/describe.py: tool_schema(s)/tool_schemas (assistant), controls (app), help and context_line(s) (agent context + human help)
pattern_mapping.Diagnoser: hubreg/diagnose.py: Diagnoser.unknown_action/unknown_option/arg_type/arg_range/arg_missing/hook_failure/confirm_required/bad_result, all reading the record and rendering a repaired call
pattern_mapping.Walker: hubreg/walker.py: Walker.walk() binds every sample, runs it, checks help/schema/controls render, redirects resolve, and result keys equal the declared fields; Registry.walk() exposes it
pattern_mapping.Bound call / warnings: hubreg/errors.py: Call (.record_name, .on, .args, .warnings) and CallWarning (.code, .message); warnings reach the CLI output next to the result

notes_applied: Note 1 (structure and consistency checks): build_record/build_arg refuse missing/unknown keys, a non-callable run, non-list fields, duplicate args, required-after-optional, untyped args, missing samples, AND semantic errors: default outside min/max, default of the wrong type, usual range outside hard limits or inverted, values on a non-enum, enum without values, option redirect to a nonexistent option, record redirect to a nonexistent action, duplicate (on,name).

Note 2 (hard limits vs usual ranges, in the declared unit): binder refuses outside [min,max] with an E_ARG_RANGE whose fix is the clamped call, and appends a W_RANGE warning (with usual_hint) when a caller-supplied value is outside `usual`; the check uses the value as written and no unit conversion happens here.

Note 3 (nothing falls back silently): unknown options are refused before missing ones, wrong types are refused (True is not a number, NaN/inf refused, nothing coerced), explicit None is a type error, and an empty string for a number is E_ARG_TYPE.

Note 4 (redirects stay in the records): method-level redirects in the record, option-level redirects in the argument spec; the diagnoser, the describer's help and the walker all read those same tables, and a repair carries the caller's values across the rename (set_temp(temp=21) -> set_temperature(target=21)).

Note 5 (walk the whole registry, results included): walk() binds and runs every sample, requires result keys to be exactly the declared fields, flags non-serialisable results and renders help/schemas; samples live in the record, so registration refuses a sample that does not bind (E_BAD_SAMPLE). Limits/warnings/redirects get their own record-generated tests in tests/test_generated.py.

Note 6 (pluggable argument types): the binder knows no types; ArgType.accepts/schema/describe, and a domain Colour type is added in the tests through Registry(arg_types=...) with schemas and help following automatically.
Note 7 (one record per receiver kind and name): storage is keyed by (on, name), so the same action name on two kinds is two records (tested); the lookup returns a single record, no overloading.

Note 8 (defaults are part of identity): defaults are validated against the declared limits and are rendered in help, tool schemas, controls and repair hints; renames are expressed as validated redirects.

Note 9 (enumerate the exceptions): HAND_BOUND_GLOBALS is the visible list of hand-bound names, walker.check_agent_surface() proves every agent-visible name is a record (or listed) and that every record has a description; the list is empty and a test keeps it so.

Note 10 (composite operations are records too): a record's fields may be a callable of the bound arguments (some options add columns), so a composite/user-defined action is described like any other and the walker checks each call's own shape.
Extra: register_all() is atomic and resolves redirect targets inside a batch, so plug-ins can rename towards actions registered later in the same batch while single register() stays strict.
tests: 155 unittest tests in 12 files: registration structure/consistency, binding and refusals, confirmation and result shape, description (tool schemas, controls, help, context lines), the walker (clean and deliberately broken records), demo behaviour, record-generated limit/type/redirect cases, CLI via subprocess, pluggable types, callable fields and docstring doctests. Last result: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> Ran 155 tests, OK (0 failures, 0 errors).
chapter_feedback: The chapter's bind sketch processes specs before unknown keys, which would report ARG_MISSING for `set_temperature(temp=21)` and lose the near-miss repair the chapter itself asks for; I reversed the order (unknown options first) and noted it in the binder.

Where the samples belong is contradictory between chapter and task: note 5 argues for keeping sample arguments in the test file and warns that putting them in the record lets registration require them, while TASK.md puts `samples` in the record. I kept them in the record and made registration bind every sample, which is the stricter reading of the pattern.

The chapter says redirect targets must be validated at registration but never says what to do when a plug-in renames an action that is registered later (registration order is otherwise arbitrary). I had to invent `register_all` with deferred, atomic redirect checking; a sentence on batching would have saved a guess.

Option-level redirects are declared per argument spec but are semantically per record ('{ min } → use above'). It was not obvious whether the key or the value owns the redirect; I validated that each target is an existing argument name and aggregate them into one record-wide table.

The chapter's walker sketch talks about `required(declared)` (optional fields may be missing), but TASK.md declares `fields` as a plain list of result keys with no optional marker. I treat every declared field as required and report extra/missing keys as walk problems plus W_UNDECLARED_FIELD/W_MISSING_FIELD warnings at run time.

The chapter never says whether a default that sits outside the usual range should warn. Warning for it would be noise (the caller chose nothing), so I warn only for caller-supplied values and surface such defaults only in help.

The `expand` variant of a record (composite operations as graphs) is described in the Solution but has no place in TASK.md's record shape; I supported the other 'function of the bound arguments' idea (callable `fields`) and left expansion out, which left me guessing whether composites were expected.

The 'flags' participant suggests a host policy that records cannot lower; that was clear and easy to implement, but the chapter does not say whether the confirmation refusal should carry a `fix` — I gave it `confirmed=True` appended to the repaired call, which the CLI honours as `--confirmed`.

The chapter's claim that a redirect beats the nearest name, and that both are shown when they differ, was the single most useful sentence for the diagnoser; the rest of the refusal wording (which pieces to include, punctuation, how to render a fixed call) I had to design.
